messages:
Ana R.: Hey team — customer ACME is reporting a spike of 403s starting ~10:20 UTC after we rolled keys. They rotated their API key via the self-serve UI and then got widespread 403s for a subset of requests. Not all regions affected. Logs: 403 x-req-id=abc123 (repro link: https://internal/trace/abc123) :eyes:
Matt L.: Thanks Ana. Are these server-to-server server keys or browser keys?
Ana R.: Server keys (per-service). They use our hosted API, not private. They said traffic hitting us from eu-west-1 is OK; us-east-1 sees the 403s.
Julia K.: Can you paste a sample curl they used (sanitized)? Also did they rotate in Vault or via Console?
Ana R.: Rotated via Console (UI) at 10:18 UTC. Sample header they sent: `Authorization: Bearer sk-live-REDACTED` (we already redacted).
Kevin S.: I see a partial propagation event in the rotation job logs — deploy-bot shows rotation job finished but vault-bot shows rewrap stuck on one KMS alias for ~2m. Looks like the rotation flow completed in the control plane but the KMS rewrap step failed transiently and retried.
vault-bot: rewrap-failure: alias arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111:alias/redwood-key rewrap attempt 1 failed: ThrottlingException
Ana R.: So why would that cause 403s only in us-east-1 and not eu-west?
Matt L.: Two possibilities: 1) Our regional cache (edge API gateway) has a cached token->policy mapping in us-east that wasn't evicted. 2) Long-lived worker processes (env var) in some of the customer's infra or our sidecar kept the old key in memory.
Julia K.: Can we confirm exact error body from our auth service? Is it "invalid_api_key" or "revoked_key"?
Ana R.: Error body: `{\"error\":\"invalid_api_key\",\"reason\":\"not-found\"}`. So our auth layer didn't find the new key mapping in the datastore.
Kevin S.: That aligns with a partial write: control plane updated Console and DB in eu-west but db write or KV metadata didn't land in us-east region replicas due to a race while KMS rewrap was failing. Also, our auth cache TTL is 60s; edge caches might be sticky longer because of unhealthy cache invalidation path.
Matt L.: Immediate mitigation for customer: ask them to do either (A) retry requests (we can force a short ttl poke), or (B) rotate to a newly created key instead of reusing alias — but that's annoying. Better: we can trigger a targeted cache invalidation and push a background repair job to rewrap the key after the KMS quota window.
Ana R.: Can ops run these quick commands?
Kevin S.: Yes, ops runbook steps:
```
# Check rotation job status
kubectl -n redwood get jobs rotation-job-196234 -o yaml
# Force cache flush on edge nodes (us-east)
curl -X POST https://edge-internal.us-east-1/flush-cache -H "Authorization: Bearer $EDGE_ADMIN"
# Re-run rewrap with exponential backoff
aws kms rewrap --ciphertext-blob fileb://ciphertext.bin --source-key-id alias/old --destination-key-id alias/new --region us-east-1
```
Matt L.: I'm pushing a hotfix to the rotation worker to mark keys "pending" until KMS rewrap confirms across all regions. PR #4521 rolling now. deploy-bot: starting canary deploy to us-east.
deploy-bot: canary-deploy: rotation-worker v2.7.3 -> v2.7.4 started (canary: 2 pods in us-east).
Ana R.: I asked the customer to retry after 10m and to share curl -v for any failing request. They sent back a trace where Authorization header was still the new key but we returned 403.
Julia K.: That suggests our auth DB doesn't return the mapping even though Console shows the key present. Can you check DB replication lag?
Kevin S.: Replication lag metric spike at 10:19 in us-east: WAL apply lag peaked ~135s due to a transient CPU spike on one replica. The rotation write landed on primary but didn’t fully apply to that replica before edge routing kept using it.
Ana R.: OK. Resolution steps we did:
- Forced cache flush on us-east edge nodes
- Manually retried KMS rewrap with backoff and it succeeded at 10:24
- Ran a repair job to reapply key metadata to replica nodes
- Asked customer to retry; they reported success and no more 403s
Matt L.: Postmortem actions: add circuit to mark rotation incomplete until KMS step returns success across all regions; increase monitoring on KMS throttling and DB apply lag; add a post-rotation probe that hits a small test route to validate key resolves in every region.
Julia K.: Also a user-facing improvement: show rotation status in UI with a "fully propagated" indicator and ETA.
Ana R.: Customer comms: I sent a short note: "Thanks — we found a transient rewrap+replication race causing partial 403s. We flushed caches and repaired replicas; please reopen if you see more errors." They replied :thumbsup:.
Kevin S.: Capture runbook as KBA and link to ticket. Also we should recommend customers using long-lived processes to restart after rotation (or watch for our webhook notifications).
Ana R.: I'll close the support ticket in 24h if no regressions. Notes saved to internal case 78921.
Julia K.: Good work. Quick follow-up: can we add a small retry on client SDKs for 403->invalid_api_key that polls for 20s then fails? Might reduce noise for short propagation blips.
Matt L.: I'll add an SDK issue.
Ana R.: Closing thread for now. Thanks all.
